questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
Multiple aspects were crucial for my choice of Bologna as my exchange destination. First of all, University of Bologna is one of the oldest universities in the world and has a very positive reputation. This historical aspect made it interesting for me to visit the university. The faculty of economics also have several connections to my home university which ensured for me that the academic level was of a high standard.
Moreover, the culture in Bologna, especially in terms of food and wine, of course was very attracting to me.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: A wonderful city with many students. The city center is full of life any day of the week. The university is great. I can only recommend going to Bologna.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I had no problems finding the necessary information. The website of the university is very informative.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I did not recieve any assistance

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Quite hard. One needs to be prepared to spend more than expected on housing to find something, especially if you do not want to live in a shared room or shared apartment

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Start looking early on and be aware of fraughts

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: If willing to spend 1000 euro a month one can find nice housing and living just outside the city center is no problem. The university is accessible by bike or foot from almost anywhere in the city.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Upon arrival I booked a Teams-meeting with the university, who registrered my arrival and provided me with the necessary information.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Information about correct registration in courses, exams etc

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was registrered in all classes that I wanted

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: At least at the faculty of economics one should not worry about getting the courses they want.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level is very high and almost the same level as the University of Copehagen

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: We had some mandatory student presentations in some of the courses. Besides this the style of teaching was very similar

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Advanced Behavioral Economics, Financial Market Regulation, Structural Macroeconometrics, Public Economics and Advanced Time Series Econometrics

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Structural Macroeconometrics was a very good course with a great professor. The course has a good balance between the theoretical part and applied part of econometrics.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: The opening of the apartment I was supposed to move into upon arrival was postponed by 3 weeks

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Housing. As told earlier this is the only thing to be aware of if going on exhcange in Bologna. Housing is difficult to find and is more expensive than expected. However, look outside the city center and buy a bike upon arrival or use the bus. It is easy getting around in city

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Great possibilities to meet up with other students and play a football match, padel, tennis etc

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot of different clubs for different sports. However, easier to arrange matches with people yourself.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I did not make use of any of these. I found my own connections by going out in the city center and meeting up with some of the many international students

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Visit other cities in Italy. Going around by train is cheap and fast. Also some cheap flights to Sicilia is available from Bologna.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. No problems since the city and the university is very international

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just go out and be open to new friendships. Ask some of your classmates if they want to go out and grab a beer

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The restaurant culture. The restaurants are fully booked every weekend with localsl. The atmosphere at all restaurants are great.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Make sure to leave space in your budget to eat out, visit other italian cities and start looking for housing in well advance

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not besides what already told

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The many great experiences in the evenings and during trips which created friendships for life.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Housing

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
